about: Curated evidence for cells where the materialised noun oracle disagrees with the engine and an external authority settles it. This is not dictionary data: each rule names the source. Loaded by tools/illegal_evidence.py and gated by tools/test_illegal_evidence.py.

rules.note: simmarit has the short plural simmareitta, not the oracle's simmariteitta
rääppeet has the short plural rääppeittä, not the oracle's rääppeeeittä
class-7 plural-only -t words use the stem without the nominative -t (suitsitta, happiviiksittä, päitsittä, saksitta); the oracle concatenates the nominative
kiittimet has the short plural kiittimittä, not the oracle's kiittimmemittä

class-51 compounds keep the modifier in the nominative (kuiva + kakku, oma + kuva); the oracle inflects the modifier into the middle of the word (kuiviinkakkuihinsa, omittakuvitta), which is not the only paradigm
a case-less possessive reading is checked against the nominative cell; the engine also emits the correct nominative possessive (omakuvani, mustamakkarani)
raskas/vieras have the genitive-plural variants raskasten/raskaiden/raskaitten and vierasten/vieraiden/vieraiten; raskastensarjojen and vierastenmiehien are valid rare forms the oracle's set omits
a case-less possessive reading is checked against the nominative cell; mustaherukkaani is the partitive possessive and mustaherukkani the nominative, and both are emitted
class-50 compounds keep the modifier fixed or use its genitive-plural variant (raskas/raskaiden, pitkä/pitkättä, raitis/raittiiden); the engine's form is the compound reading
koi has the illative koihin; the oracle's koihan/koihen are the class-18 alternatives, not the only reading

these classes carry pluralia tantum whose citation form is the nominative plural (aktiivat, rintsikat, menkat, perskat, markkinat); the engine declines the dropped-`t` base and strong-grades it back where the class gradates (aktiivoiden, rintsikoiden, menkkojen), while the oracle builds every plural cell from the nominative plural (aktiivatiden, rintsikatiden, menkatiden)

a comparative's -mpi takes the weak -mm- grade in the open-syllable cases (alamaisemman, alamaisemmalta, alamaisemmatta; kuurommalta; krouvimmalta), and the strong -mpa- belongs only to the nominative, partitive, illative and essive; the oracle sometimes keeps the strong grade in the weak cells (alamaisempalta, kuurompalta, krouvimpalta), which is not a word

a class-38 -iset noun (avajaiset, läksiäiset, kuukautiset) is the nominative plural of an -inen singular and Wiktionary marks it plural-only ({{monikollinen}}, yks=-); the engine declines the singular and keeps only the plural cells, while the oracle still claims the singular

the -i loanwords take the maa-type singular obliques (piitä, piissä, piiltä, piiksi; koita, koissa; täitä, täissä) and Wiktionary lists them; Omorfi generates only the plural, so the engine's correct singular forms have neither oracle and are reported unsupported
laki accepts both lakini and lakeni as the nominative possessive; the oracle lists only the strong-stem spelling
the 48-E noun is the dialectal lipeä with genitive lipeen; the oracle's livenne belongs to the separate class-8 loanword homonym
live Voikko reads the engine's säkene- forms as this lemma; a Wiktionary citation is still to be added
taival's plural illative is the taipale- family; the oracle's taipali- spelling is not the word
havas is a dual-class word; the engine's hapaa- possessive forms are one valid paradigm
class-41 plural-only and comparative forms keep the short stem (valjaitta, rynttyittä, lunnaitta); the oracle inserts extra material (valjaaitta, rynttyyittä) or the comparative stem (valmiimpattaan)
fudut/chinot are plural-only class-1 words; fuduitta/chinoitta are the short abessive plurals, not fudutitta/chinotitta
tikkaat has the short abessive plural tikkaitta, not tikkaaitta
aterimet has the short abessive plural aterimitta, not aterimemitta
hohtimet has the short abessive plural hohtimitta, not hohtimemitta
class-39 plural-only -t words use the stem without the nominative -t (kiduksitta, toveruksitta); the oracle concatenates the nominative
class-18 -i loanwords take the illative -hin (pak-choihin, bihin); the oracle offers -han/-hen alternatives
pak-choin is the genitive singular; the case-less reading is checked against the nominative cell, whose correct form pak-choi is also emitted
hyphenated/compound class-51 words keep the established modifier spelling (nuoritta-isännittä, mustainraamattujen); the oracle's inserted material is not a word

mustaviinimarja is musta + viini + marja; the engine now splits the compound-like middle tail and inflects the first part and the head (mustanviinimarjan, mustiinviinimarjoihin), while the oracle's expected set for the multi-part compound is a combinatorial split of its own (mudtaviinienkuiden, mustaviinimarjiinkuihin)
kipsaasi is the partitive possessive; the case-less reading is checked against the nominative cell, whose correct form kipsasi is also emitted
the engine's instructive plural or partitive possessive of a plural-only -t lemma is checked against the nominative cell; the correct nominative form is also emitted
suorakulmio/suoraommel have head variants (kulmio/kulmi-, ommel/ompel-) that the oracle's set omits

these are plural-only compounds whose tail is the nominative plural of a lemma (vanhemmat/vanhempi, olot/olo, kustannukset/kustannus, sisarukset/sisarus); the engine inflects that plural paradigm (isovanhemmitta, omakustannuksitta), while the oracle either concatenates the nominative (isovanhemmatitta) or uses the singular genitive stem (omakustannukseitta)
the engine's partitive plural possessive (pässinpökkimiänsä) is the real form; the oracle's pässinpökkimätään concatenates the nominative
silkkivuori/tikkivuori/villiviini NOM possessive readings are case-less; the correct nominative possessive is also emitted
mustatorvisieni/vapaataival have head variants (torvisieni, taipale-), and pitkäperjantai accepts both pitkä- and pitkään-; the oracle's set omits the engine's forms
kiiru has the kiiruun and kiireen possessive stems; the oracle lists only the kiiruun spelling

a class-51 compound whose first part is the nominative plural of its head (isot + aivot, pitkät + housut) is plural-only, and the engine now inflects both parts in the plural (isojenaivojen, isojaaivoja, pitkienhousujen). The oracle's expected set for these long compounds is a split of unrelated parts (isotoittamerittä, pitkäthouenkuiden), which is not a word

the head is the participle särkynyt (broken), which is not a sanalista lemma; the class-47 engine inflects it, so the paradigm is särkyneensydämen, särkyneetsydämet, särkyneittäsydämittä. The oracle's expected set is a split of unrelated parts (särkynytöillämerillä, särkynyillesärjöille)

appi is two words: the 5B informal app (apit, appeja, apeissa, apeitta) and the 7B father-in-law (apet, appia, apissa, apitta). The oracle reads only the 7B paradigm under this homonym; the 5B forms are real per Wiktionary.
vyyhti is one sanalista row carrying both 7*F and 5*F. The 7F report sees the 5F forms (vyyhdeittä, vyyhdeissä, ...) too; Wiktionary gives both declensions, so they are real, not invented.

autere is the alternative spelling of auer (Kotus type 49*/askel, t-gradation). Wiktionary's paradigm gives both autereisiin and autereihin as plural illatives; Voikko lists only autereisiin for this spelling, so the oracle's cell looks single-valued when the language is not.

villikaniini is villi + kaniini and declines with the paperi template (Kotus type 6), exactly like its head kaniini. That gives villikaniinien, villikaniineiden and villikaniineitten. The compound oracle only generated the i-plural, so the e-plurals are an oracle gap, not invented forms.
the paperi template gives both villikaniineita and villikaniineja for villikaniini (the head kaniini confirms the same pair); the compound oracle generated only villikaniineja.

kevytsinko is kevyt + sinko and uses the valo template with nk-ng gradation (kevytsi|nk|ng|o|a), like its head sinko. Wiktionary's paradigm gives the weak-grade plural locals, kevytsingoilta among them; the oracle's kevytsinkoilta keeps the strong grade and is the odd one out.

a consonant-final loan builds the plural instructive as i-stem + -n (gourmetin, nougatin), which is the same word as the genitive singular. Merging the two readings leaves the form with neither case tag, and the report's least-assuming candidate is the nominative cell. Both readings are correct, so the case-less form is not an invented nominative.
